title.zh: 卷一百二十七 列傳第七十七: 姚令言 張光晟 源休 喬琳 張涉 蔣鎮 洪經綸 彭偃
title.en: Volume 127 Biographies 77: Yao Lingyan, Zhang Guangcheng, Yuan Xiu, Qiao Lin, Zhang She, Jiang Zhen, Hong Jinglun, Peng Yan
title.raw: 卷一百二十七 列傳第七十七: 姚令言 張光晟 源休 喬琳 張涉 蔣鎮 洪經綸 彭偃 Volume 127 Biographies 77: Yao Lingyan, Zhang Guangcheng, Yuan Xiu, Qiao Lin, Zhang She, Jiang Zhen, Hong Jinglun, Peng Yan

sentences.zh: 姚令言，河中人也。

translations.literal: Yao Lingyan was a native of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Lingyan was from Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 少應募，起於卒伍，隸涇原節度馬璘。

translations.literal: In youth he answered a recruitment call, rose from the ranks of common soldiers, and served under the Jingyuan military commissioner Ma Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted while young, rose from the ranks, and served under Ma Lin, military commissioner of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 以戰功累授金吾大將軍同正，為衙前兵馬使，改試太常卿、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: For successive battle merits he was repeatedly appointed acting Jinwu Grand General, made yamen-front military commissioner, and transferred to provisional Grand Master of Ceremonies while also serving as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Battlefield honors brought him repeated promotions to acting Jinwu Grand General and yamen-front military commissioner, then to provisional Grand Master of Ceremonies with concurrent appointment as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 建中元年，孟暤為涇原節度留後，自以文吏進身，不樂軍旅，頻表薦令言謹肅，堪任將帥。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong, Meng Hui served as acting Jingyuan military commissioner; considering himself a career civil official, he had no taste for military affairs and repeatedly memorialized that Lingyan was sober and dutiful and fit to command troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 1 (780), Meng Hui was acting military commissioner of Jingyuan. A civil official by background, he disliked military command and repeatedly recommended Lingyan as sober, reliable, and fit to lead troops.

sentences.zh: 暤尋歸朝廷，遂拜令言為四鎮北庭行營涇原節度使、涇州刺史、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Before long Meng Hui returned to court, and Lingyan was appointed military commissioner of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign command for Jingyuan, prefect of Jing Prefecture, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Hui soon returned to the capital, and Lingyan was appointed Jingyuan military commissioner of the Four Garrisons Northern Court campaign command, prefect of Jing, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 建中四年，李希烈叛，寇陷汝州，詔哥舒曜率師攻之，營於襄城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong, Li Xilie rebelled, raided, and captured Ru Prefecture; an edict ordered Ge Shuya to lead troops against him and encamp at Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 4 (783), Li Xilie rebelled and seized Ru Prefecture. The court ordered Ge Shuya to attack him and encamped at Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 希烈兵數萬圍襄城，勢甚危急。

translations.literal: Li Xilie's forces, numbering tens of thousands, besieged Xiangcheng; the situation was extremely perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie mustered tens of thousands of men to besiege Xiangcheng, and the crisis was acute.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔令言率本鎮兵五萬赴援。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, an edict ordered Lingyan to lead fifty thousand troops of his own command in relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the court ordered Lingyan to march fifty thousand men of his own command to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 涇師離鎮，多攜子弟而來，望至京師以獲厚賞，及師上路，一無所賜。

translations.literal: The Jing troops left their garrison, many bringing sons and younger relatives, hoping that on reaching the capital they would receive lavish rewards—but once the army was on the march, nothing was bestowed at all.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing army left its post with many men bringing wives and children, expecting rich rewards once they reached the capital—but after they set out, they received nothing.

sentences.zh: 時詔京兆尹王翃犒軍士，唯糲食菜啖而已，軍士覆而不顧，皆憤怒，揚言曰：「吾輩棄父母妻子，將死於難，而食不得飽，安能以草命捍白刃耶！

translations.literal: At the time an edict had ordered Wang Hong, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, to feast the troops, but they were given only coarse grain and vegetables to eat; the soldiers overturned the food and paid no heed, all furious, shouting: "We have abandoned parents, wives, and children and will die in hardship, yet we cannot eat our fill—how can we risk our worthless lives against naked blades!"
translations.idiomatic: The court had ordered Wang Hong, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, to reward the troops, but they were fed only coarse grain and vegetables. The men overturned the food and refused it, raging aloud: "We left parents, wives, and children behind to die in battle, and we cannot even eat our fill—why should we throw away our lives against cold steel?"

sentences.zh: 國家瓊林、大盈，寶貨堆積，不取此以自活，何往耶？

translations.literal: "The state's Qionlin and Daying treasuries are piled with valuables—if we do not take these to keep ourselves alive, where else shall we go?"
translations.idiomatic: "The imperial treasuries at Qionlin and Daying are heaped with treasure—if we will not take that to live on, where else can we turn?"

sentences.zh: 」行次浐水，乃返戈，大呼鼓噪而還。

translations.literal: When they reached Chan River on the march, they turned their weapons about, shouting and drumming boisterously as they returned.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the Chan River they reversed their weapons, shouting and beating drums as they marched back.

sentences.zh: 令言曰：「比約東都有厚賞，兒郎勿草草，此非求活之良圖也。

translations.literal: Lingyan said: "It was agreed that when we reach the eastern capital there would be rich rewards—men, do not act rashly; this is not a sound plan for survival."
translations.idiomatic: Lingyan said, "We were promised rich rewards in the eastern capital—men, do not act rashly; this is no good way to save yourselves."

sentences.zh: 」眾不聽，以戈環令言請退，令言急奏之。

translations.literal: The crowd would not listen; they surrounded Lingyan with spears and pressed him to withdraw, and he urgently reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The troops would not listen. They ringed Lingyan with spears and pressed him to step aside, and he sent an urgent report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上恐，令內庫出繒彩二十車馳賜之，軍聲浩浩，令言不能戢。

translations.literal: The emperor was alarmed and ordered twenty cartloads of silk from the inner treasury sent posthaste as gifts, but the army's clamor was deafening and Lingyan could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the emperor ordered twenty cartloads of silk rushed from the inner treasury as gifts, but the army's uproar was overwhelming and Lingyan could not quiet them.

sentences.zh: 街市居人狼狽走竄，亂兵呼曰：「勿走，不稅汝間架矣！

translations.literal: Market residents fled in panic and disorder; the mutinous troops shouted: "Do not run—we will not levy your chamber-and-rafter tax!"
translations.idiomatic: Shopkeepers and townspeople fled in panic while the mutineers shouted, "Do not run—we will not collect your housing tax!"

sentences.zh: 」德宗令普王與學士姜公輔往撫勞之，才出內門，賊已斬關，陣於丹鳳樓下。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong ordered Prince Pu and academician Jiang Gongfu to go comfort and reward them, but they had barely passed the inner gate when the rebels had already broken through the pass and arrayed below Danfeng Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong sent Prince Pu and academician Jiang Gongfu to reassure the troops, but they had barely left the inner gate when the rebels had forced the gates and formed ranks below Danfeng Tower.

sentences.zh: 是日，德宗倉卒出幸，賊縱入府庫輦運，極力而止。

translations.literal: That day Dezong fled in haste; the rebels were allowed into the treasury stores and carted goods away until forcibly stopped.
translations.idiomatic: That day Dezong fled the capital in haste. The rebels poured into the treasuries and hauled away goods until they were stopped by force.

sentences.zh: 時太尉硃泚罷鎮居晉昌裏第，是夜，叛卒謀曰：「硃太尉久囚於宅，若迎為主，大事濟矣。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Mentor Zhu Ci, having been dismissed from his command, lived at his mansion in Jinchang Lane; that night the mutinous soldiers plotted: "Grand Mentor Zhu has long been confined in his residence—if we welcome him as our leader, the great enterprise will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor Zhu Ci had been stripped of his command and was living at his mansion in Jinchang Lane. That night the mutineers plotted: "Grand Mentor Zhu has been shut up in his house too long—if we make him our leader, the cause will succeed."

sentences.zh: 」泚嘗節制涇州，眾知其失權，廢居怏怏，又幸泚寬和，乃請令言率騎迎泚於晉昌裏。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci had once commanded Jing Prefecture; the troops knew he had lost power and lived in forced retirement, ill at ease—they also counted on Zhu Ci's mild and placid manner, and so asked Lingyan to lead cavalry to welcome Zhu Ci from Jinchang Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci had once governed Jing Prefecture. The men knew he had lost office and brooded in retirement; they also trusted his mild temper, and asked Lingyan to lead cavalry to bring Zhu Ci from Jinchang Lane.

sentences.zh: 泚初遲疑，以食飼之，徐觀眾意，既而諸校齊至，乃自第張炬火入居含元殿。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci at first hesitated; they fed him food while he slowly gauged the crowd's intent, and when the various officers had all arrived, he left his mansion with torches ablaze and took up residence in Hanyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci hesitated at first. They fed him while he watched the mood of the troops; when the officers had all gathered, he left his house with torches blazing and entered Hanyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 既僭號，乃以令言為侍中，與源休同知賊政事。

translations.literal: Once he had usurped the imperial title, he appointed Lingyan Grand Counselor and had him share with Yuan Xiu the management of rebel administration.
translations.idiomatic: After he declared himself emperor, he made Lingyan Grand Counselor and had him administer rebel affairs jointly with Yuan Xiu.

sentences.zh: 既以身先逆亂，頗盡心於賊，害宗室，圍奉天，皆令言為首帥也。

translations.literal: Having personally led the rebellion at the forefront, he devoted himself zealously to the rebel cause; harming the imperial clan and besieging Fengtian were both led by Lingyan as chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had personally led the revolt, he threw himself into the rebel cause. The slaughter of imperial clansmen and the siege of Fengtian were both commanded by Lingyan.

sentences.zh: 群兇宴樂，既醉，令言與源休論功，令言自此蕭何，源休曰：「帷幄之謀，成秦之業，無出予之右者。

translations.literal: When the rebels were feasting and merry, once drunk Lingyan and Yuan Xiu debated their merits; Lingyan claimed to be Xiao He from this point onward, and Yuan Xiu said: "In stratagems from within the tent, in accomplishing the enterprise of Qin, none surpasses me."
translations.idiomatic: At a rebel feast, once drunk Lingyan and Yuan Xiu argued over their merits. Lingyan declared himself Xiao He henceforth. Yuan Xiu said, "In counsel from the tent and in founding the Qin enterprise, no one ranks above me."

sentences.zh: 吾比蕭何無讓，子當曹參可矣。

translations.literal: "Compared with Xiao He I yield nothing—you may serve as Cao Can."
translations.idiomatic: "I yield nothing to Xiao He—you can be Cao Can."

sentences.zh: 」時朝士在賊廷者，聞之皆笑，謂源休為火迫酂侯。

translations.literal: Court officials then at the rebel court heard this and all laughed, calling Yuan Xiu "the Marquis of Zan driven by fire"—a pun on Xiao He's title sounding like "burned marquis."
translations.idiomatic: Court officials trapped in the rebel court heard this and laughed, dubbing Yuan Xiu "the Marquis of Zan pressed by fire"—a pun on Xiao He's title that also suggested a marquis scorched by flame.

sentences.zh: 硃泚敗，令言與張廷芝尚有眾萬人，從泚將入吐蕃。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci was defeated, Lingyan and Zhang Tingzhi still had a force of ten thousand and followed Zhu Ci intending to enter Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci was defeated, Lingyan and Zhang Tingzhi still commanded ten thousand men and followed Zhu Ci, intending to flee into Tibet.

sentences.zh: 至涇州，欲投田希鑒，希鑒偽致禮誘之，與泚俱斬首來獻。

translations.literal: Reaching Jing Prefecture, they wished to surrender to Tian Xijian; Tian Xijian feigned courtesy to lure them in and together with Zhu Ci beheaded them and presented their heads.
translations.idiomatic: At Jing Prefecture they tried to surrender to Tian Xijian. Tian Xijian pretended courtesy to lure them in, then beheaded them along with Zhu Ci and sent their heads to the court.

sentences.zh: 張光晟，京兆盩厔人，起於行間。

translations.literal: Zhang Guangcheng was a native of Zhouzhi in Jingzhao, rising from the marching ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangcheng was from Zhouzhi in metropolitan Jingzhao and rose from the ranks on campaign.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，哥舒翰兵敗潼關，大將王思禮所乘馬中流矢而斃，光晟時在騎卒之中，因下，以馬授思禮。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, when Geshu Han's army was defeated at Tong Pass, the great general Wang Silun's mount was struck midstream by an arrow and fell; Guangcheng was then among the cavalrymen, dismounted, and gave his horse to Silun.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianbao era Geshu Han's army was routed at Tong Pass. The great general Wang Silun's horse was struck by an arrow in midstream and fell. Guangcheng, then among the cavalry, dismounted and gave his own mount to Silun.

sentences.zh: 思禮問其姓名，不告而退，思禮陰記其形貌，常使人密求之。

translations.literal: Silun asked his name; he would not tell and withdrew. Silun secretly noted his appearance and often sent men to search for him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Silun asked his name, but he refused to say and slipped away. Silun memorized his face and often sent men to search for him in secret.

sentences.zh: 無何，思禮為河東節度使，其偏將辛雲京為代州刺史，屢為將校譖毀，思禮怒焉。

translations.literal: Before long Silun became military commissioner of Hedong; his lieutenant Xin Yunjing served as prefect of Dai Prefecture and was repeatedly slandered by fellow officers, and Silun grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Silun became military commissioner of Hedong. His subordinate Xin Yunjing was prefect of Dai and was repeatedly slandered by other officers until Silun grew furious.

sentences.zh: 雲京惶懼，不知所出。

translations.literal: Yunjing was fearful and at a loss what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Yunjing was terrified and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 光晟時隸雲京麾下，因間進曰：「光晟素有德於王司空，比不言諸，恥以舊恩受賞。

translations.literal: Guangcheng was then under Yunjing's command and took occasion to advance, saying: "Guangcheng once did a kindness for Minister Wang and has until now said nothing of it, ashamed to trade on an old favor for reward.
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng was then serving under Yunjing and spoke up privately: "I once did Wang the Minister a service. I have never spoken of it, for I would be ashamed to claim reward for an old favor.

sentences.zh: 今使君憂迫，光晟請奉命一見司空，則使君之難可解。

translations.literal: Now that my lord is in distress, Guangcheng asks leave to go on your orders and see the Minister once—then my lord's difficulty can be resolved."
translations.idiomatic: Now that you are in distress, let me go on your orders and see the Minister once. Your trouble can then be resolved."

sentences.zh: 」雲京然其計，即令之太原。

translations.literal: Yunjing approved his plan and at once sent him to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yunjing agreed to the plan and sent him at once to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 乃謁思禮，未及言舊，思禮識之，遽曰：「爾豈非吾故人乎？

translations.literal: He then called on Silun; before he could speak of the past, Silun recognized him and at once said: "Are you not my old acquaintance?
translations.idiomatic: He called on Silun. Before he could mention the past, Silun recognized him and cried, "Are you not my old friend?

sentences.zh: 何相見之晚也！

translations.literal: Why have we met so late!"
translations.idiomatic: Why did we meet so late!"

sentences.zh: 」光晟遂陳潼關之事，思禮大喜，因執其手感泣曰：「吾有今日，子之力也。

translations.literal: Guangcheng then related the affair at Tong Pass; Silun was greatly pleased, took his hand, and wept, saying: "That I have today is your doing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng told the story of Tong Pass. Silun was overjoyed, seized his hand, and wept: "I owe my life today to you.

sentences.zh: 求子頗久，竟此相遇，何慰如之？

translations.literal: I have sought you long; to meet at last—what comfort could be greater?"
translations.idiomatic: I have searched for you a long time. To meet you at last—what greater comfort could there be?"

sentences.zh: 」命同榻而坐，結為兄弟。

translations.literal: He ordered them to sit on the same couch and swore brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: He had them sit on the same couch and sworn as brothers.

sentences.zh: 光晟遂述雲京之屈，思禮曰：「雲京比涉謗言，過亦不細，今為故人，特舍之矣。

translations.literal: Guangcheng then told of Yunjing's grievance. Silun said: "Yunjing has indeed been involved in slanderous talk and his fault is not slight—but for an old friend's sake I will specially pardon him."
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng then explained Yunjing's plight. Silun said, "Yunjing has indeed been tangled in slander, and his fault is not small—but for your sake I will let it go."

sentences.zh: 」即日擢光晟為兵馬使，賚田宅、縑帛甚厚，累奏特進，試太常少卿，委以心腹。

translations.literal: That same day he promoted Guangcheng to military commissioner, bestowed fields, houses, and silk in great abundance, repeatedly memorialized for his special advancement, appointed him provisional Vice Minister of Ceremonies, and entrusted him as a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he promoted Guangcheng to military commissioner, gave him fields, houses, and lavish gifts of silk, repeatedly recommended him for special advancement, appointed him provisional Vice Minister of Ceremonies, and treated him as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 及雲京為河東節度使，又奏光晟為代州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yunjing became military commissioner of Hedong, he again memorialized to appoint Guangcheng prefect of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunjing became military commissioner of Hedong, he again recommended Guangcheng as prefect of Dai.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，遷單於都護、兼御史中丞、振武軍使。

translations.literal: At the end of the Dali era he was transferred to be protector-general of Chanyu, with concurrent appointment as Vice Censor-in-Chief and commissioner of the Zhenwu army.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dali era he was appointed protector-general of Chanyu, with concurrent posts as Vice Censor-in-Chief and commissioner of the Zhenwu army.

sentences.zh: 代宗密謂之曰：「北蕃縱橫日久，當思所禦之計。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong told him in secret: "The northern barbarians have ranged freely for a long time—you must think of measures to check them."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong told him privately, "The northern tribes have run rampant for years. You must find a way to hold them in check."

sentences.zh: 」光晟既受命，至鎮，威令甚行。

translations.literal: Once Guangcheng had received his commission and reached his post, his authority and orders were strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guangcheng took up the post, his authority was firmly enforced.

sentences.zh: 建中元年，回紇突董梅錄領眾並雜種胡等自京師還國，輿載金帛，相屬於道。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong, the Uyghur Tudun Meilu led his followers together with various mixed Hu peoples returning from the capital to their country, carts laden with gold and silk stretching in unbroken succession along the road.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 1 (780), the Uyghur leader Tudun Meilu led his men and various other Hu groups home from the capital, their carts piled with gold and silk in an endless line along the road.

sentences.zh: 光晟訝其裝橐頗多，潛令驛吏以長錐刺之，則皆輦歸所誘致京師婦人也。

translations.literal: Guangcheng was surprised that their baggage was so ample and secretly ordered relay clerks to pierce it with long awls; inside were all women they had enticed and brought back from the capital in carts.
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng was struck by how heavy their baggage was and secretly had relay clerks pierce the packs with long awls. Inside were women they had lured from the capital and were hauling home in carts.

sentences.zh: 遂給突董及所領徒悉令赴宴，酒酣，光晟伏甲盡拘而殺之，死者千余人，唯留二胡歸國復命。

translations.literal: He then invited Tudun and all his followers to a feast; when the wine was deep, Guangcheng's hidden armed men seized and killed them all—more than a thousand dead—keeping only two Hu to return home and report.
translations.idiomatic: He invited Tudun and all his followers to a banquet. When they were drunk, Guangcheng's hidden troops seized and killed them—more than a thousand dead—sparing only two Hu to carry the report back to their country.

sentences.zh: 遂部其婦人，給糧還京，收其金帛，賞賚軍士。

translations.literal: He then organized the women, gave them grain, and sent them back to the capital; he seized their gold and silk and used them to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the women back to the capital with provisions, seized their gold and silk, and used the spoils to reward his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 後回紇遣使來訴，上不欲甚阻蕃情，征拜右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Later the Uyghurs sent envoys to protest; the emperor did not wish to alienate the tribes too greatly and summoned Guangcheng to appointment as Right Jinwu General.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghurs sent envoys to protest, the court did not wish to estrange them further and recalled Guangcheng to serve as Right Jinwu General.

sentences.zh: 回紇猶怨懟不已，又降為睦王傅，尋改太仆卿，負才怏怏不得誌。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs still nursed resentment without end, and he was demoted again to tutor of the Prince of Mu, then transferred to Grand Master of the Stud; talented and resentful, he could not fulfill his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs remained bitter, and he was demoted again to tutor of the Prince of Mu, then made Grand Master of the Stud. Talented but thwarted, he brooded over his frustrated ambitions.

sentences.zh: 賊泚僭逆，署光晟偽節度使兼宰相。

translations.literal: When the rebel Zhu Ci usurped power, he appointed Guangcheng false military commissioner and concurrent chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled and seized power, he appointed Guangcheng rebel military commissioner and chancellor.

sentences.zh: 及泚眾頻敗，遂擇精兵五千配光晟，營於九曲，去東渭橋凡十餘里。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci's forces suffered repeated defeats, he selected five thousand elite troops and assigned them to Guangcheng, encamped at Jiuqu, a little more than ten li from East Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Ci's army suffered repeated defeats, he gave Guangcheng five thousand picked troops and encamped them at Jiuqu, a little over ten li from East Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 光晟潛使於李晟，有歸順之意。

translations.literal: Guangcheng secretly sent word to Li Sheng, showing an intention to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng secretly contacted Li Sheng, signaling his wish to defect.

sentences.zh: 晟進兵入苑，光晟勸賊泚宜速西奔，光晟以數千人送泚出城，因率眾回降於晟。

translations.literal: When Sheng advanced into the imperial park, Guangcheng urged the rebel Zhu Ci to flee west at once; Guangcheng escorted Zhu Ci out of the city with several thousand men, then led his troops back to surrender to Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: As Sheng advanced into the imperial park, Guangcheng urged Zhu Ci to flee west immediately. He escorted Zhu Ci out of the city with several thousand men, then turned his troops about and surrendered to Sheng.

sentences.zh: 晟以其誠款，又愛其材，欲奏用之，俾令歸私第，表請特減其罪。

translations.literal: Sheng, because of his sincere submission and also cherishing his talent, wished to memorialize for his employment, had him return to his private residence, and submitted a memorial asking special reduction of his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng valued his sincere surrender and admired his ability. He wanted to recommend him for office, sent him to his private residence, and petitioned for a special reduction of his punishment.

sentences.zh: 每大宴會，皆令就坐，華州節度使駱元光詬之曰：「吾不能與反虜同席！

translations.literal: At every great banquet he was told to take a seat, but Luo Yuanguang, military commissioner of Hua Prefecture, reviled him, saying: "I cannot sit at the same table with a rebel traitor!"
translations.idiomatic: At every grand feast Sheng had him take a seat, but Luo Yuanguang, military commissioner of Hua, reviled him: "I will not sit at table with a rebel!"

sentences.zh: 」拂衣還營。

translations.literal: He brushed his robes and returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: He swept his robes aside and returned to camp.

sentences.zh: 晟不得已，拘之私第，後有詔言其狀跡不可原，乃斬之。

translations.literal: Sheng had no choice but to detain him in his private residence; later an edict declared that his conduct could not be pardoned, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had no choice but to confine him at his residence. Later an edict declared his crimes beyond pardon, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 源休，相州臨漳人，京兆尹光輿之子也。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiu was a native of Linzhang in Xiang Prefecture and the son of Guangyu, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu was from Linzhang in Xiang Prefecture and the son of Guangyu, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 休以幹局，累授監察御史、殿中侍御史、青苗使判官，遷虞部員外郎，。

translations.literal: Xiu, for his competence, was repeatedly appointed investigating censor, palace censor, and aide to the Green Sprouts commissioner, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Parks and Forests Office.
translations.idiomatic: For his administrative ability Xiu rose through the ranks as investigating censor, palace censor, and aide to the Green Sprouts commissioner, then was promoted to Vice Director of the Parks and Forests Office.

sentences.zh: 出潭州刺史，入為主客郎中，遷給事中、御史中丞、左庶子。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Tan Prefecture, entered court as director of the Hosts and Guests Bureau, and was promoted to supervising secretary, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Left Vice Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Tan, then returned to the capital as director of the Hosts and Guests Bureau and was promoted to supervising secretary, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Left Vice Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 其妻即吏部侍郎王翊女也。

translations.literal: His wife was the daughter of Wang Yi, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was the daughter of Wang Yi, Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 因小忿而離，妻族上訴，下御史臺驗理，休遲留不答款狀，除名，配流溱州。

translations.literal: Because of a small quarrel they separated; his wife's clan appealed to the throne, and the case was sent to the Censorate for investigation. Xiu delayed and would not answer the written interrogatory; he was struck from the rolls and banished to Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a petty quarrel they separated. His wife's kin appealed to the throne, and the Censorate was ordered to investigate. Xiu stalled and refused to answer the formal interrogatory. He was expelled from office and exiled to Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，移岳州。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was transferred to Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建中初，楊炎執政，以京兆尹嚴郢威名稍著，心欲傾之。

translations.literal: Early in Jianzhong, when Yang Yan held power, Yan Ying as metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao had begun to win a certain reputation, and Yang Yan wished in his heart to bring him down.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong, with Yang Yan in power, Yan Ying as metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao was gaining a reputation, and Yang Yan resolved to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 郢，即王翊甥婿也。

translations.literal: Ying was Wang Yi's nephew by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was Wang Yi's nephew by marriage.

sentences.zh: 休與王氏離絕之時，炎風聞休、郢有隙，遂擢休自流人為京兆少尹，俾令伺郢過失。

translations.literal: When Xiu and the Wang clan had broken off relations, Yang Yan had heard that Xiu and Ying bore a grudge, and so promoted Xiu from exile to be metropolitan vice-prefect of Jingzhao, ordering him to watch for Ying's faults.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu and the Wang family had fallen out, Yang Yan heard that Xiu and Ying were at odds. He recalled Xiu from exile to be metropolitan vice-prefect of Jingzhao and ordered him to spy on Ying's missteps.

sentences.zh: 休既職久，與郢親善，炎怒之，奏令以本官兼御史中丞，奉使回紇。

translations.literal: After Xiu had long held office he became close with Ying; Yang Yan was angry and memorialized that he should keep his present post while also serving as Vice Censor-in-Chief on a mission to the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiu had been in office for some time he grew friendly with Ying. Yang Yan was furious and had him sent to the Uyghurs as envoy while retaining his post with concurrent appointment as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 休至振武，軍使張光晟已殺回紇突董等，上初欲遂絕其使，令休還，待命於太原。

translations.literal: When Xiu reached Zhenwu, army commissioner Zhang Guangcheng had already killed the Uyghur Tudun and others; at first the emperor wished to break off relations entirely and ordered Xiu to return, awaiting orders at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu reached Zhenwu, army commissioner Zhang Guangcheng had already killed Tudun and the other Uyghur leaders. The emperor first considered cutting off relations entirely and ordered Xiu back to await instructions at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 久之方遣，仍令休歸其突董、翳密施大小梅錄等四屍。

translations.literal: Only after a long delay was he sent forth, and he was still ordered to return the four corpses—Tudun, Yimishi, and the great and small Meilu.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long delay was he sent on his way, still charged with returning the four corpses: Tudun, Yimishi, and the great and small Meilu.

sentences.zh: 突董者，即武義可汗之叔父也。

translations.literal: Tudun was the uncle of the Wuyi Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Tudun was the uncle of the Wuyi Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 屍既至，可汗令宰臣已下具彩服車馬來迎。

translations.literal: When the corpses arrived, the qaghan ordered chancellors and officials below them to come out in colored robes with carriages and horses to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: When the bodies arrived, the qaghan ordered his ministers and officials to meet them in colored robes with carriages and horses.

sentences.zh: 其宰相頡於思迦坐大帳，立休等於帳外雪中，詰殺突董等故。

translations.literal: His chancellor Xieyusijia sat in the great tent and had Xiu and the others stand in the snow outside the tent, interrogating them on the reason for killing Tudun and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Xieyusijia sat in the great tent and had Xiu and his party stand in the snow outside, demanding to know why Tudun and the others had been killed.

sentences.zh: 休曰：「突董等自與張光晟忿鬥而死，非天子命也。

translations.literal: Xiu said: "Tudun and the others died in a quarrel with Zhang Guangcheng of their own accord—it was not by the Son of Heaven's command."
translations.idiomatic: Xiu said, "Tudun and the others died in a private quarrel with Zhang Guangcheng. It was not by imperial order."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「使者背唐國，負罪當死，不能自戮耶？

translations.literal: They asked again: "The envoy has betrayed Tang and bears guilt deserving death—can you not kill yourselves?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked again, "You have betrayed Tang and deserve death. Will you not kill yourselves?"

sentences.zh: 不然，何假手於我殺之也？

translations.literal: If not, why borrow our hands to kill them?"
translations.idiomatic: If not, why make us do your killing for you?"

sentences.zh: 」凡將殺者數矣，言頗悖慢，乃引去，供餼甚薄，留之五十余日，乃得還。

translations.literal: Several times they were on the verge of being killed; their words were quite insolent. They were led away, provisions were very meager, and they were detained more than fifty days before they could return.
translations.idiomatic: Several times they were nearly executed. Their replies were insolent. They were led away, given scant provisions, and held for more than fifty days before they were allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 可汗使謂休曰：「我國人皆欲殺汝，唯我不然。

translations.literal: The qaghan's envoy said to Xiu: "All my countrymen wish to kill you—only I do not."
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan's envoy told Xiu, "Everyone in my country wants you dead—only I do not."

sentences.zh: 汝國已殺突董等，吾又殺汝，猶以血洗血，汙益甚爾。

translations.literal: "Your state has already killed Tudun and the others; if I kill you too, it is still washing blood with blood—the stain grows only worse."
translations.idiomatic: "Your court has already killed Tudun and the others. If I kill you as well, that is only washing blood with blood—the stain grows worse."

sentences.zh: 吾今以水洗血，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: "I now wash blood with water—is that not better!"
translations.idiomatic: "I would rather wash blood away with water—is that not better?"

sentences.zh: 所欠吾馬直絹一百八十萬疋，當速歸之。

translations.literal: "The silk owed us for horse payments—one million eight hundred thousand bolts—must be returned at once."
translations.idiomatic: "The one million eight hundred thousand bolts of silk still owed for our horses must be paid promptly."

sentences.zh: 」遣散支將軍康赤心等隨休來朝，休竟不得見其可汗。

translations.literal: He sent the general Kang Chixin of the Sanzhi branch and others to accompany Xiu to court; Xiu never obtained an audience with the qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Kang Chixin of the Sanzhi branch and others to accompany Xiu to court. Xiu never obtained an audience with the qaghan.

sentences.zh: 尋遣赤心等歸，與之帛十萬疋、金銀十萬兩，償其馬直。

translations.literal: Before long Chixin and the others were sent back, given one hundred thousand bolts of silk and one hundred thousand taels of gold and silver to repay the horse payments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chixin and his party were sent home with one hundred thousand bolts of silk and one hundred thousand taels of gold and silver to settle the horse debt.

sentences.zh: 休履危而還，宰相盧杞又恐復命之日以口辯結恩，將至太原，遽奏為光祿卿。

translations.literal: Xiu returned after braving danger; Chancellor Lu Qi again feared that on the day of his report he would win favor by eloquent speech, and when he was about to reach Taiyuan hurriedly memorialized to appoint him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu returned after a perilous mission. Chancellor Lu Qi feared that on reporting back Xiu would win favor through his eloquence, and when Xiu was nearing Taiyuan Lu Qi hastily had him appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 休以其還使賞薄，居常怨望。

translations.literal: Xiu, because the reward for his return mission was meager, constantly harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Because his reward for the embassy was meager, Xiu nursed a constant grievance.

sentences.zh: 會涇原兵叛，立硃泚為主。

translations.literal: It happened that the Jingyuan troops rebelled and set up Zhu Ci as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingyuan army mutinied, they made Zhu Ci their leader.

sentences.zh: 初但稱太尉，朝官謁泚者，悉勸奏迎鑾駕，既不合泚意而退。

translations.literal: At first he was called only Grand Mentor; court officials who called on Zhu Ci all urged memorializing to welcome the imperial carriage back, and since this did not suit Zhu Ci's intent they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhu Ci was addressed only as Grand Mentor. Court officials who visited him all urged welcoming the emperor back to the capital, and when that did not suit Zhu Ci they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及休至，遂屏人移時，言多悖逆，盛陳成敗，稱述符命，勸令僭號。

translations.literal: When Xiu arrived, he dismissed attendants and spoke at length; his words were largely treasonous, he set forth success and failure at length, cited portents and mandates, and urged him to usurp the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu arrived he dismissed attendants and spoke at length in private. His words were treasonous: he laid out the balance of victory and defeat, cited omens and destiny, and urged Zhu Ci to declare himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 泚悅其言，以休為宰相，判度支。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci was pleased with his words and appointed Xiu chancellor with charge of the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci was pleased and made Xiu chancellor with charge of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 休遂為謀主，至於兵食軍資，遷除補擬，內外咨謀，一稟休畫。

translations.literal: Xiu then became chief strategist; as for troops, provisions, military supplies, appointments and replacements, all counsel within and without followed Xiu's plans alone.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu became the chief strategist. Troops, provisions, military supplies, appointments and replacements—every decision inside and outside the court followed his plans alone.

sentences.zh: 故時人云：「源休之逆，甚於硃泚。

translations.literal: Hence people of the time said: "Yuan Xiu's rebellion was worse than Zhu Ci's."
translations.idiomatic: People said at the time, "Yuan Xiu's treason was worse than Zhu Ci's."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷大臣之奔竄不獲者，多為休所誘致，以至戮辱，職休而為，蓋非一焉。

translations.literal: Court ministers who fled but were not able to escape were mostly lured in by Xiu, leading to slaughter and humiliation—deeds for which Xiu was responsible were more than one.
translations.idiomatic: Many court officials who tried to flee but were caught were lured back by Xiu and then slaughtered or humiliated. Such deeds attributable to Xiu were not few.

sentences.zh: 又勸泚鋤翦宗室，以絕人望，命萬年縣賊曹尉楊偡專其斷決，諸王子孫遇害不可勝數。

translations.literal: He also urged Zhu Ci to uproot the imperial clan to cut off popular hope, and appointed Yang Yan of the Wanian county bandit-suppression office to handle judgments exclusively—the princes' sons and grandsons who suffered harm were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged Zhu Ci to exterminate the imperial clan to destroy any hope of restoration, and put Yang Yan of the Wanian county bandit-suppression office in charge of the killings. The princes and their descendants who perished were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 泚敗走，休隨至寧州。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci was defeated and fled, Xiu followed him to Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci was defeated and fled, Xiu followed him to Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 泚死，休走鳳翔，為其部曲所殺，傳首來獻。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci died, Xiu fled to Fengxiang and was killed by Zhu Ci's personal troops; his head was sent in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Ci died, Xiu fled to Fengxiang, where Zhu Ci's personal troops killed him and sent his head to the court.

sentences.zh: 休三子並斬於東市，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Xiu's three sons were all executed at the eastern market, and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: All three of Xiu's sons were executed at the eastern market, and his family's property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 喬琳，太原人。

translations.literal: Qiao Lin was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Lin was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧誌學，以文詞稱。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor in youth, he was determined to study and was famed for his literary writings.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor as a youth, he devoted himself to learning and won renown for his literary skill.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，舉進士，補成武尉，累授興平尉。

translations.literal: Early in the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed defender of Chengwu, and was repeatedly promoted to defender of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he passed the jinshi examination, served as defender of Chengwu, and rose through successive appointments to defender of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度郭子儀辟為掌書記，尋拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Shuofang military commissioner Guo Ziyi recruited him as chief secretary, and before long he was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, military commissioner of Shuofang, took him on as chief secretary, and he soon became an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 琳倜儻疏誕，好談諧，侮謔僚列，頗無禮檢。

translations.literal: Lin was unconventional, unrestrained, and eccentric; he loved witty talk, mocked and jested at his colleagues, and was quite without propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was unconventional and unrestrained, fond of banter, and often mocked his colleagues with little regard for decorum.

sentences.zh: 同院御史畢耀初與琳嘲誚往復，因成釁隙，遂以公事互相告訴，坐貶巴州員外司戶。

translations.literal: His fellow censor in the same bureau, Bi Yao, at first exchanged banter and mockery with Lin, which bred a feud; they then accused each other on official business and Lin was demoted to acting registrar of Ba Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yao, a fellow censor in his bureau, traded barbs with Lin until a feud developed. They then lodged official charges against each other, and Lin was demoted to acting registrar of Ba Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遂起為南郭令，改殿中侍御史，充山南節度張獻誠行軍司馬。

translations.literal: He was then recalled as magistrate of Nanguo, transferred to palace censor, and served as campaign adjutant to Zhang Xiancheng, military commissioner of Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as magistrate of Nanguo, made palace censor, and served as campaign adjutant to Zhang Xiancheng, military commissioner of Shannan.

sentences.zh: 使罷，為劍南東川節度鮮于叔明判官。

translations.literal: When the mission ended, he became aide to Xianyu Shuming, military commissioner of eastern Sichuan in Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: When that assignment ended, he became aide to Xianyu Shuming, military commissioner of eastern Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 改檢校駕部郎中、果綿遂三州刺史、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to acting director of the Imperial Transport Bureau, prefect of the three prefectures Guo, Mian, and Su, and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting director of the Imperial Transport Bureau, prefect of Guo, Mian, and Su, and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 入為大理少卿、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He entered court as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review and libationer of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review and libationer of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 出為懷州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Huai.

sentences.zh: 琳素與張涉友善，上在春宮，涉嘗為侍讀。

translations.literal: Lin had long been friendly with Zhang She; when the emperor was crown prince, She had once served as his study companion.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had long been close to Zhang She, who had served as study companion when the emperor was crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，多以政事詢訪於涉，盛稱琳識度材略，堪備大用，因拜御史大夫、平章事。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, he often consulted She on state affairs; She lavishly praised Lin's judgment and talent as fit for great employment, and Lin was appointed Censor-in-Chief and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne, he often consulted She on affairs of state. She praised Lin's judgment and ability as fit for high office, and Lin was appointed Censor-in-Chief and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 琳本粗材，又年高有耳疾，上每顧問，對答失次，論奏不合時。

translations.literal: Lin was by nature coarse material, and moreover was advanced in years with an ear ailment; whenever the emperor questioned him, his replies were disorderly and his memorials ill suited to the times.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was a rough talent at best, and in old age suffered from deafness. Whenever the emperor questioned him, his answers were confused and his policy proposals out of step with the times.

sentences.zh: 幸居相位凡八十余日，除工部尚書，罷知政事，尋加迎皇太后副使。

translations.literal: Fortunately he held the chancellorship for only a little more than eighty days; he was appointed Minister of Works, removed from participation in government, and soon added as deputy envoy to welcome the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He held the chancellorship for only a little over eighty days before being made Minister of Works and removed from government. He was soon named deputy envoy to welcome the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 硃泚之亂，扈從至奉天，轉吏部尚書，遷太子少師。

translations.literal: During Zhu Ci's rebellion he followed the emperor to Fengtian, was transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's rebellion he accompanied the emperor to Fengtian, became Minister of Personnel, and was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 再幸梁、洋，從至盩厔，托以馬乏遲留，上以琳舊老，心敬重之，慰諭頗至，以禦馬一匹給焉。

translations.literal: On the second journey to Liang and Yang he followed as far as Zhouzhi, pleading that his horses were exhausted and he must delay; the emperor, because Lin was old and venerable, respected him in his heart, comforted him at length, and gave him an imperial horse.
translations.idiomatic: On the second flight to Liang and Yang he followed as far as Zhouzhi, then pleaded exhaustion of his horses and stayed behind. The emperor, who still respected the old man, comforted him warmly and gave him an imperial horse.

sentences.zh: 又懇辭以老疾不堪山阻登頓，上悵然，賜之所執策曰：「勉為良圖，與卿決矣。

translations.literal: He again begged off, saying his age and illness could not bear mountain barriers and steep climbing; the emperor was sorrowful and bestowed the whip he held, saying: "Strive for a good plan—I take leave of you."
translations.idiomatic: He begged again, saying age and illness left him unable to endure mountain passes. The emperor sighed and gave him the whip in his hand, saying, "Take care of yourself. This is our parting."

sentences.zh: 」後數日，乃削發為僧，止仙遊寺。

translations.literal: Several days later he shaved his head and became a monk, residing at Xianyou Temple.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he shaved his head, became a monk, and took up residence at Xianyou Temple.

sentences.zh: 賊泚聞之，遂令數十騎追至京城，俾為偽吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the rebel Zhu Ci heard of this, he sent several dozen horsemen to pursue him to the capital and compelled him to serve as false Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci heard of it, he sent several dozen horsemen to bring Lin back to the capital and forced him to serve as rebel Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 令源休被公服，饋肉食，琳雖辭讓，而僧言求施。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiu was ordered to don official robes and present meat food; Lin declined, but in monk's speech begged for alms.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu was told to dress Lin in official robes and offer him meat. Lin declined, but in his monk's guise asked for alms instead.

sentences.zh: 琳掌賊中吏部，選人前請曰：「所註某官不穩便。

translations.literal: Lin managed the rebel Ministry of Personnel; a candidate came forward and said: "The office you have assigned me is not secure."
translations.idiomatic: Lin ran the rebel Ministry of Personnel. A candidate came to him and said, "The post you assigned me is not secure."

sentences.zh: 」琳謂之曰：「足下謂此選竟穩便乎？

translations.literal: Lin said to him: "Do you think this round of appointments will be secure at all?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin replied, "Do you think any appointment in this regime is secure?"

sentences.zh: 」及官軍收京師，當處極刑，時琳已七十余，李晟憫其衰老，表請減死。

translations.literal: When the imperial army recovered the capital he was due for the extreme penalty; Lin was then over seventy, and Li Sheng pitied his old age and memorialized asking reduction of the death sentence.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army retook the capital, Lin faced execution. He was over seventy, and Li Sheng, pitying his age, petitioned to spare his life.

sentences.zh: 上以其累經重任，頓虧臣節，自受逆命，頗聞譏諧悖慢之言，背義負恩，固不可舍，命斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he had repeatedly held weighty office yet suddenly violated ministerial integrity, had of his own accord accepted rebel commands, and was widely reported to have spoken in mockery, insolence, and disrespect, betraying righteousness and failing in gratitude—could by no means be spared—and ordered his execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that Lin, having held high office repeatedly, had violated his duty, accepted rebel commands of his own accord, and was known for mocking, insolent speech. Having betrayed his obligations, he could not be spared, and the emperor ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 臨刑嘆曰：「喬琳以七月七日生，亦以此日死，豈非命歟！」

translations.literal: Facing execution he sighed: "Qiao Lin was born on the seventh day of the seventh month and also dies on this day—is it not fate!"
translations.idiomatic: At the block he sighed, "Qiao Lin was born on the seventh day of the seventh month and dies on it as well—is this not destiny?"

sentences.zh: 張涉者，蒲州人，家世儒者。

translations.literal: Zhang She was a native of Pu Prefecture, from a family of Confucian scholars for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang She was from Pu Prefecture, from a long line of Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 涉依國學為諸生講說，稍遷國子博士，亦能為文，嘗請有司日試萬言，時呼張萬言。

translations.literal: She relied on the Directorate of Education to lecture students, was gradually promoted to erudite of the Imperial University, and could also write; he once asked the authorities for a daily examination of ten thousand characters, and at the time was called Zhang Ten Thousand Words.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured students at the Directorate of Education, rose to erudite of the Imperial University, and was a capable writer. He once asked the authorities to test him at ten thousand characters a day, earning the nickname Zhang Ten Thousand Words.

sentences.zh: 德宗在春宮，受經於涉。

translations.literal: When Dezong was in the Eastern Palace, he received the classics from She.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong was crown prince, he studied the classics under She.

sentences.zh: 及即位之夕，召涉入宮，訪以庶政，大小之事皆咨之。

translations.literal: On the night he took the throne he summoned She into the palace, consulted him on general administration, and sought his advice on matters great and small.
translations.idiomatic: On the night he took the throne he summoned She to the palace and consulted him on every matter of government, large and small.

sentences.zh: 翌日，詔居翰林，恩禮甚厚，親重莫比。

translations.literal: The next day an edict placed him in the Hanlin Academy; favor and ceremony were very generous, and none was more intimate or esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was ordered into the Hanlin Academy with lavish favor. No one was closer to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 自博士遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: From erudite he was promoted to attendant cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from erudite to attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 上方屬意宰輔，唯賢是擇，故求人於不次之地。

translations.literal: The emperor was then intent on chancellors and chose only the worthy, and so sought men from extraordinary channels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was intent on finding worthy chancellors and searched for talent outside the usual channels.

sentences.zh: 涉舉懷州刺史喬琳為相，上授之不疑，天下聞之者皆愕然。

translations.literal: She recommended Qiao Lin, prefect of Huai, as chancellor; the emperor appointed him without doubt, and all who heard of it throughout the realm were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: She recommended Qiao Lin, prefect of Huai, for chancellor. The emperor appointed him without hesitation, and the whole empire was astonished.

sentences.zh: 數月，琳以不稱職罷，上由是疏涉。

translations.literal: After several months Lin was removed for incompetence, and from this the emperor grew distant from She.
translations.idiomatic: Within months Lin was dismissed as unfit for office, and the emperor grew distant from She.

sentences.zh: 俄受前湖南都團練使辛京杲贓事發，詔曰：「尊師之道，禮有所加；

translations.literal: Before long the bribery case of the former military training commissioner of Hunan, Xin Jinggao, came to light, and an edict said: "In honoring one's teacher, ritual adds something;
translations.idiomatic: Soon the bribery case of the former Hunan military training commissioner Xin Jinggao came to light. An edict declared, "In honoring one's teacher, ritual grants special consideration;

sentences.zh: 議故之法，恩有所掩。

translations.literal: in discussing the law for old services, grace may cover something."
translations.idiomatic: and in weighing past service, mercy may cover faults."

sentences.zh: 張涉賄賂交通，頗駭時聽，常所親重，良深嘆惜。

translations.literal: Zhang She took bribes and maintained improper connections, which greatly shocked public opinion; one whom he had often favored and esteemed—deep indeed was the regret.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang She had taken bribes and maintained improper connections, shocking public opinion. The emperor deeply regretted having favored a man he had once held so close.

sentences.zh: 宜放歸田裏。」

translations.literal: He should be released to return to his fields."
translations.idiomatic: He is to be released and sent home to his fields."

sentences.zh: 蔣鎮，常州義興人，尚書左丞洌之子也。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhen was a native of Yixing in Chang Prefecture and the son of Jiang Lie, Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhen was from Yixing in Chang Prefecture and the son of Jiang Lie, Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 與兄練並以文學進。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Lian both advanced through literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Lian both rose through literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 天寶末舉賢良，累授左拾遺、司封員外郎，轉諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he was recommended as worthy and good, was repeatedly appointed Left Reminder, Vice Director of the Seals and Investitures Bureau, and transferred to remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianbao he was recommended as worthy and good, served as Left Reminder and Vice Director of the Seals and Investitures Bureau, and became a remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 時戶部侍郎、判度支韓滉上言：「河中鹽池生瑞鹽，實土德之上瑞。

translations.literal: At the time Han Huang, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue with charge of the treasury, memorialized: "The salt ponds of Hezhong have produced auspicious salt—truly a supreme omen of the virtue of Earth."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Han Huang, Vice Minister of Revenue with charge of the treasury, memorialized, "The salt ponds of Hezhong have produced auspicious salt—a supreme omen of the virtue of Earth."

sentences.zh: 」上以秋霖稍多，水潦為患，不宜生瑞，命鎮馳驛檢行之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because autumn rains had been rather heavy and flooding was a calamity, held that it was not fitting for omens to appear, and ordered Zhen to go posthaste by relay to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, noting heavy autumn rains and widespread flooding, thought it unfitting that omens should appear and ordered Zhen to inspect the site by urgent relay.

sentences.zh: 鎮奏與滉同，仍上表賀，請宣付史館，並請置神祠，錫其嘉號寶應靈慶池。

translations.literal: Zhen memorialized in agreement with Huang, also submitted a congratulatory memorial, asked that it be proclaimed to the Historiography Office, and requested establishment of a spirit shrine, bestowing the fine name Precious Response Spirit Celebration Pond.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen reported as Huang had, submitted a congratulatory memorial, asked that the event be recorded in the Historiography Office, and requested a spirit shrine with the honorific name Precious Response Spirit Celebration Pond.

sentences.zh: 地霖潦彌月，壞居人廬舍非一，鹽池為潦水所入，其味多苦。

translations.literal: The land had suffered flooding rains for a full month, destroying many dwellings of the inhabitants; floodwater entered the salt ponds and their taste was largely bitter.
translations.idiomatic: Flooding had lasted a full month, destroying many homes. Floodwater had entered the salt ponds, and the salt tasted mostly bitter.

sentences.zh: 韓滉慮鹽戶減稅，詐奏雨不壞池，池生瑞鹽，鎮庇之飾詐，識者醜之。

translations.literal: Han Huang, fearing reduced salt-tax from the salt households, falsely memorialized that rain did not harm the ponds and that the ponds produced auspicious salt; Zhen shielded him and embellished the fraud—those who knew were ashamed of it.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang, fearing reduced salt tax revenue, falsely reported that rain had not harmed the ponds and that auspicious salt had appeared. Zhen covered for him and dressed up the fraud. Men of judgment despised them both.

sentences.zh: 轉給事中、工部侍郎，以簡儉稱於時。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretary and Vice Minister of Works, and was famed at the time for simplicity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supervising secretary and Vice Minister of Works and was known at court for simplicity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 其妹婿源溥，即休之弟也，以姻媾之故，與休交好。

translations.literal: His sister's husband was Yuan Pu, younger brother of Yuan Xiu; because of the marriage tie, Zhen was on friendly terms with Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: His sister's husband was Yuan Pu, younger brother of Yuan Xiu. Through this marriage tie Zhen was friendly with Xiu.

sentences.zh: 涇師之叛，鎮潛竄，夜至鄠縣西，馬躓墮溝澗中，傷足不能進。

translations.literal: When the Jing troops rebelled, Zhen fled in secret; by night he reached west of E County, his horse stumbled and fell into a ditch ravine, injuring his foot so he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing army rebelled, Zhen fled in secret. By night he reached west of E County, where his horse stumbled into a ravine and injured his foot so that he could go no farther.

sentences.zh: 時史練已與源休相率受賊偽官。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Lian had already followed Yuan Xiu in accepting false offices from the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shi Lian had already followed Yuan Xiu in accepting rebel appointments.

sentences.zh: 鎮仆人有逃歸投練，雲鎮病足在鄠。

translations.literal: Zhen's servant fled back and surrendered to Lian, reporting that Zhen lay ill of foot at E.
translations.idiomatic: One of Zhen's servants escaped and reported to Lian that Zhen lay injured at E.

sentences.zh: 練與源休聞之大喜，遂言於賊泚此。

translations.literal: Lian and Yuan Xiu heard this with great joy and reported it to the rebel Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Lian and Yuan Xiu were delighted and told the rebel Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 泚素慕鎮清名，即令騎二百求之鄠縣西。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci had long admired Zhen's pure reputation and at once sent two hundred horsemen to seek him west of E County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci had long admired Zhen's reputation and sent two hundred horsemen to find him west of E County.

sentences.zh: 明日，擁鎮而至，署為偽宰相。

translations.literal: The next day they escorted Zhen in and appointed him false chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they brought Zhen in and appointed him rebel chancellor.

sentences.zh: 既知不免，每憂沮，常懷刃將自裁，多為兄練所救而罷。

translations.literal: Once he knew he could not escape, he was constantly dejected; he often carried a blade intending suicide, but was mostly stopped by his elder brother Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not escape, he was constantly despondent and often carried a blade to kill himself, but his brother Lian usually stopped him.

sentences.zh: 數日後，復謀竄匿，竟以性懦畏怯，計終不果。

translations.literal: Several days later he again plotted to flee and hide, but in the end because of his timid and fearful nature the plan never came to fruition.
translations.idiomatic: Days later he plotted to flee again, but his timid nature kept him from carrying the plan through.

sentences.zh: 然源休與泚頻議，欲逼脅潛藏衣冠，大加殺戮，鎮輒力爭救，獲全者甚眾。

translations.literal: Yet Yuan Xiu and Zhu Ci frequently discussed forcing hidden court officials into service and slaughtering them on a large scale; Zhen repeatedly argued strenuously to save them, and very many were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu and Zhu Ci often discussed hunting down hidden officials and killing them in large numbers. Zhen repeatedly argued to spare them, and many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 至是，與兄練等並授偽職，斬於東市西北街。

translations.literal: At this time he, his elder brother Lian, and the others who had all accepted false offices were executed at the northwest street of the eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he, his brother Lian, and others who had accepted rebel offices were executed at the northwest corner of the eastern market.

sentences.zh: 初鎮父洌，叔渙，當祿山、思明之亂，並授偽職，然以家風修整，為士大夫所稱。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhen's father Lie and uncle Huan, during the rebellions of Lushan and Siming, had both accepted false offices, yet because the family style was well ordered they were praised by scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's father Lie and uncle Huan had both accepted false offices during the rebellions of An Lushan and Shi Siming, yet their household was so well ordered that scholar-officials still praised them.

sentences.zh: 鎮兄弟亦以教義禮法為己任，而貪祿愛死，節隳身戮，為天下笑。

translations.literal: The Jiang brothers also took instruction in righteousness and ritual law as their charge, yet clung to salary and loved life; their integrity was destroyed and their persons slaughtered, and they became the laughter of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang brothers too professed devotion to righteousness and ritual, yet clung to office and feared death. Their integrity was ruined, their lives forfeited, and they became a laughingstock throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 洪經綸，建中初為黜陟使。

translations.literal: Hong Jinglun, early in Jianzhong, served as promotion-and-demotion commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Jinglun served early in Jianzhong as promotion-and-demotion commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至東都，訪聞魏州田悅食糧兵凡七萬人，經綸素昧時機，先以符停其兵四萬人，令歸農畝。

translations.literal: Reaching the eastern capital, he learned on inquiry that Tian Yue of Weizhou had grain-paid troops totaling seventy thousand; Jinglun, who had never understood the times, first issued an order disbanding forty thousand of his troops and ordering them back to the fields.
translations.idiomatic: At the eastern capital he learned that Tian Yue of Weizhou maintained seventy thousand grain-paid troops. Jinglun, who had no sense of the political moment, first ordered forty thousand men disbanded and sent back to farming.

sentences.zh: 田悅偽順命，即依符罷之；

translations.literal: Tian Yue falsely obeyed the command and at once dismissed them according to the order;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue pretended to obey and dismissed them as ordered;

sentences.zh: 而大集所罷兵士，激怒之曰：「爾等在軍旅，各有父母妻子，既為黜陟使所罷，如何得衣食？

translations.literal: but then gathered the dismissed soldiers in great numbers and incited them, saying: "You are in the army, each with parents, wives, and children—now that the promotion-and-demotion commissioner has dismissed you, how will you get food and clothing?"
translations.idiomatic: then gathered the dismissed troops and inflamed them: "You serve in the army with parents, wives, and children at home. Now the promotion commissioner has dismissed you—how will you feed and clothe yourselves?"

sentences.zh: 」遂大哭。

translations.literal: They then wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: They burst into loud weeping.

sentences.zh: 悅乃盡出家財衣服厚給之，各令還其部伍，自此人堅叛心，由是罷職。

translations.literal: Yue then gave out all his family wealth in clothing as generous gifts, ordered each back to his unit, and from this the men's resolve to rebel was firm; Jinglun was removed from office for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Yue gave them lavish gifts from his family wealth and sent each man back to his unit. From that day their loyalty to rebellion was fixed, and Jinglun was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 及硃泚反，偽授太常少卿。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he was falsely appointed Vice Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he was given the false title of Vice Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 彭偃，少負俊才，銳於進取，為當塗者所抑，形於言色。

translations.literal: Peng Yan in youth possessed outstanding talent, was keen to advance, was suppressed by those in power, and showed it in speech and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yan was gifted in youth, ambitious, and openly resentful of the powerful men who blocked his rise.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，為都官員外郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali he was Vice Director of the Capital Offices Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dali era he served as Vice Director of the Capital Offices Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時劍南東川觀察使李叔明上言，以「佛、道二教，無益於時，請粗加澄汰。

translations.literal: At the time Li Shuming, observation commissioner of eastern Sichuan in Jiannan, memorialized that "the two teachings of Buddhism and Daoism are of no benefit to the age and should be roughly clarified and reduced."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Shuming, observation commissioner of eastern Sichuan, memorialized that Buddhism and Daoism were of no benefit to the age and should be roughly reduced in scale.

sentences.zh: 其東川寺觀，請定為二等：上寺留僧二十一人；

translations.literal: For monasteries and abbeys in eastern Sichuan, he asked that they be fixed in two grades: upper monasteries would retain twenty-one monks;
translations.idiomatic: For monasteries and abbeys in eastern Sichuan he proposed two grades: upper monasteries would keep twenty-one monks;

sentences.zh: 上觀留道士十四人，降殺以七，皆精選有道行者，余悉令返初。

translations.literal: upper abbeys would retain fourteen Daoist priests, with reductions by sevens at lower grades; all were to be carefully selected men of the Way in practice, and the rest were all ordered to return to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: upper abbeys fourteen Daoist priests, with reductions by sevens at lower grades. Only proven practitioners were to remain; all others were to return to lay life.

sentences.zh: 蘭若、道場無名者皆廢。

translations.literal: Lanruo chapels and Daoist halls without established names were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Unregistered chapels and halls were to be abolished entirely.

sentences.zh: 」德宗曰：「叔明此奏，可為天下通制，不唯劍南一道。

translations.literal: Dezong said: "Shuming's memorial can serve as a general regulation for the realm, not only for the Jiannan circuit alone."
translations.idiomatic: Dezong said, "Shuming's proposal can serve as a general regulation for the whole empire, not only for Jiannan."

sentences.zh: 」下尚書集議。

translations.literal: It was sent down to the Ministry of Civil Office for collective deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to the Ministry of Civil Office for collective deliberation.

sentences.zh: 偃獻議曰：

translations.literal: Yan submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yan submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 王者之政，變人心為上，因人心次之，不變不因，循常守固者為下。

translations.literal: In the government of a true king, transforming people's hearts is highest, following people's hearts is next, neither transforming nor following is lower, and clinging to the usual and guarding the fixed is lowest.
translations.idiomatic: In the government of a true king, transforming the people's hearts ranks highest, following their hearts ranks next, doing neither ranks lower, and clinging blindly to convention ranks lowest.

sentences.zh: 故非有獨見之明，不能行非常之事。

translations.literal: Therefore without vision that sees alone, one cannot carry out extraordinary affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Without singular vision, one cannot carry out extraordinary measures.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以惟新之政，為萬代法，若不革舊風，令歸正道者，非也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, with renewing government as law for ten thousand generations—if you do not reform old customs and bring them back to the correct Way, that would be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's renewing government is meant to set law for ten thousand generations. If old abuses are not reformed and brought back to the correct Way, the effort will fail.

sentences.zh: 當今道士，有名無實，時俗鮮重，亂政猶輕。

translations.literal: Today's Daoist priests have name without substance; the age scarcely esteems them, and their disorder of government is still slight.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Daoist priests are nominal rather than real. The age scarcely esteems them, and their harm to government is still slight.

sentences.zh: 唯有僧尼，頗為穢雜。

translations.literal: Only monks and nuns are quite foul and mixed.
translations.idiomatic: Only monks and nuns are truly numerous and corrupt.

sentences.zh: 自西方之教，被於中國，去聖日遠，空門不行五濁，比丘但行粗法。

translations.literal: Since the teaching from the West spread in China, the days from the sage grow distant; the empty gate does not practice the five defilements, and bhikṣus practice only coarse dharma.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Western teaching spread in China, the age has grown distant from the sage. The clergy no longer uphold the pure precepts, and monks practice only the crudest observances.

sentences.zh: 爰自後漢，至於陳、隋，僧之廢滅，其亦數乎！

translations.literal: From Later Han down to Chen and Sui, the abolition and extinction of monks—has it not occurred repeatedly!
translations.idiomatic: From Later Han through Chen and Sui, the suppression and extinction of the clergy—has this not happened again and again?

sentences.zh: 或至坑殺，殆無遺余。

translations.literal: At times it reached pit slaughter, leaving scarcely any survivors.
translations.idiomatic: At times they were slaughtered by the pitful until scarcely any survived.

sentences.zh: 前代帝王，豈惡僧道之善如此之深耶？

translations.literal: Did emperors of former ages hate the goodness of monks and Daoists so deeply?
translations.idiomatic: Did emperors of former ages hate the goodness of monks and Daoists so deeply?

sentences.zh: 蓋其亂人亦已甚矣。

translations.literal: It is rather that their disordering of the people had already gone very far.
translations.idiomatic: Rather, their harm to the people had already gone very far.

sentences.zh: 且佛之立教，清凈無為，若以色見，即是邪法，開示悟入，唯有一門，所以三乘之人，比之外道。

translations.literal: Moreover, in establishing his teaching the Buddha was pure, tranquil, and non-active; if one sees by form, that is already heterodox dharma. To open, show, awaken, and enter—there is only one gate; therefore those of the three vehicles are compared with outer ways.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha's teaching was pure, tranquil, and free of striving. To cling to appearances is already heterodox. Enlightenment admits only one gate; hence even followers of the three vehicles are classed with outer ways.

sentences.zh: 況今出家者皆是無識下劣之流，縱其戒行高潔，在於王者，已無用矣，況是茍避征徭，於殺盜淫，無所不犯者乎！

translations.literal: How much more are today's renunciants all ignorant and base riffraff—even if their precepts and conduct were lofty and pure, to a king they would already be useless; how much more those who evade corvée and taxes and violate killing, theft, and lust without exception!
translations.idiomatic: Today's clergy are ignorant and base. Even if some kept lofty precepts, they would be useless to the throne—and how much more those who flee taxes and corvée and violate every prohibition against killing, theft, and lust!

sentences.zh: 今叔明之心甚善，然臣恐其奸吏詆欺，而去者未必非，留者不必是，無益於國，不能息奸。

translations.literal: Now Shuming's intent is very good, yet I fear that corrupt clerks will slander and deceive: those dismissed may not be wrong, those retained may not be right—it will not benefit the state and cannot quell wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming's intent is admirable, but I fear corrupt officials will twist the policy. Those expelled may not be the worst offenders, and those retained may not be the best. The measure will not benefit the state or end abuse.

sentences.zh: 既不變人心，亦不因人心，強制力持，難致遠耳。

translations.literal: Since it neither transforms people's hearts nor follows people's hearts, forcibly holding it by power will be hard to carry far.
translations.idiomatic: Because it neither transforms hearts nor follows them, enforcing it by brute power will not last.

sentences.zh: 臣聞天生烝人，必將有職，遊行浮食，王制所禁。

translations.literal: I have heard that Heaven gives birth to the multitude and each must have an occupation; wandering and eating without labor is forbidden by royal institutions.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Heaven gives birth to the multitude and assigns each a calling. Wandering idlers who live without labor are forbidden by royal law.

sentences.zh: 故有才者受爵祿，不肖者出租征，此古之常道也。

translations.literal: Therefore the talented receive titles and salary, the unworthy pay rent and tax—this is the constant Way of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The talented receive rank and salary; the unworthy pay rent and tax. This is the constant Way of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 今天下僧道，不耕而食，不織而衣，廣作危言險語，以惑愚者。

translations.literal: Today monks and Daoists throughout the realm eat without plowing and clothe themselves without weaving; they widely make alarming and dangerous words to delude the foolish.
translations.idiomatic: Today's monks and Daoists eat without farming and dress without weaving. They spread alarming words to delude the foolish.

sentences.zh: 一僧衣食，歲計約三萬有余，五丁所出，不能致此。

translations.literal: One monk's food and clothing, reckoned yearly, comes to more than thirty thousand; the output of five households cannot reach this.
translations.idiomatic: A single monk's food and clothing cost more than thirty thousand cash a year—more than five farming households can produce.

sentences.zh: 舉一僧以計天下，其費可知。

translations.literal: Take one monk and calculate for the realm—the expense can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolate from one monk to the whole empire, and the cost is plain.

sentences.zh: 陛下日旰憂勤，將去人害，此而不救，奚其為政？

translations.literal: Your Majesty toils in worry until sundown, intending to remove harm to the people—if you do not remedy this, what is government for?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty toils until sundown to remove harm from the people. If you do not remedy this, what is government for?

sentences.zh: 臣伏請僧道未滿五十者，每年輸絹四疋；

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully asks that monks and Daoists under fifty years of age pay four bolts of silk yearly;
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully propose that monks and Daoists under fifty pay four bolts of silk each year;

sentences.zh: 尼及女道士未滿五十者，每年輸絹二疋；

translations.literal: nuns and female Daoist priests under fifty pay two bolts of silk yearly;
translations.idiomatic: nuns and female Daoist priests under fifty pay two bolts of silk each year;

sentences.zh: 其雜色役與百姓同。

translations.literal: their miscellaneous corvée duties would be the same as commoners'.
translations.idiomatic: and their miscellaneous corvée duties would be the same as those of commoners.

sentences.zh: 有才智者令入仕，請還俗為平人者聽。

translations.literal: Those with talent and wisdom would be ordered to enter office; those who ask to return to lay life as ordinary persons would be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent would be urged to enter office, and those who wished to return to lay life would be permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 但令就役輸課，為僧何傷。

translations.literal: Only require them to perform corvée and pay levies—what harm is there in being monks?
translations.idiomatic: If they perform corvée and pay taxes, what harm is there in their remaining monks?

sentences.zh: 臣竊料其所出，不下今之租賦三分之一，然則陛下之國富矣，蒼生之害除矣。

translations.literal: Your servant privately estimates their payments would be no less than one-third of present rent and tax—then Your Majesty's state would be rich and harm to the common people would be removed.
translations.idiomatic: I estimate their payments would amount to at least one-third of present rent and tax. The treasury would grow rich and the people's burden would be lifted.

sentences.zh: 其年過五十者，請皆免之。

translations.literal: Those over fifty years of age, I ask that they all be exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Those over fifty, I ask, should all be exempted.

sentences.zh: 夫子曰：「五十而知天命。

translations.literal: The Master said: "At fifty one knows Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "At fifty one knows Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 」列子曰：「不班白，不知道。

translations.literal: Liezi said: "Without gray hair, one does not know the Way."
translations.idiomatic: Liezi said, "Without gray hair, one does not know the Way."

sentences.zh: 」人年五十，嗜欲巳衰，縱不出家，心已近道，況戒律檢其情性哉！

translations.literal: When a person is fifty, appetites and desires have already declined; even if he does not leave home, his heart is already near the Way—how much more when precepts restrain his disposition!
translations.idiomatic: At fifty one's appetites have already waned. Even without leaving home, the heart is near the Way—how much more when precepts restrain the passions!

sentences.zh: 臣以為此令既行，僧道規避還俗者固已太半。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that once this order is enforced, monks and Daoists who evade it by returning to lay life will surely be more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Once this order is enforced, more than half the clergy will surely return to lay life to avoid it.

sentences.zh: 其年老精修者，必盡為人師，則道、釋二教益重明矣。

translations.literal: Those old in years and refined in practice will all become teachers of men, and then the two teachings of Dao and Buddha will be the more honored and clarified.
translations.idiomatic: Those who are old and truly devoted will become teachers, and the Daoist and Buddhist traditions will shine all the brighter.

sentences.zh: 議者是之，上頗善其言。

translations.literal: Those who deliberated approved it, and the emperor was quite pleased with his words.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberators approved his proposal, and the emperor was quite pleased with it.

sentences.zh: 大臣以二教行之已久，列聖奉之，不宜頓擾，宜去其太甚，其議不行。

translations.literal: Great ministers held that the two teachings had long been practiced and successive sage emperors honored them; they should not be suddenly disturbed—only the excessive should be removed—and the proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers argued that the two faiths had long been practiced and honored by successive emperors, and should not be suddenly disturbed—only excesses should be trimmed. The proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 偃以才地當掌文誥，以躁求為時論所抑，郁郁不得誌。

translations.literal: Yan by talent and standing ought to have managed literary edicts, but because of impatient striving was suppressed in public opinion, depressed and unable to fulfill his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: By talent Yan ought to have held charge of literary edicts, but his impatient striving earned him public disdain, and he brooded over his frustrated ambitions.

sentences.zh: 涇師之亂，從駕不及，匿於田家，為賊所得。

translations.literal: During the Jing troops' rebellion he could not keep up with the imperial entourage, hid in a farming household, and was seized by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jing army rebellion he failed to keep up with the imperial flight, hid on a farm, and was captured by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 硃泚素知之，得偃甚喜，偽署中書舍人，僭號辭令，皆偃為之。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci had long known him; obtaining Yan he was greatly pleased, falsely appointed him Secretariat Drafter, and all usurpation proclamations and orders were composed by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci knew him well and was delighted to capture him. He made Yan rebel Secretariat Drafter, and Yan composed all the rebel proclamations and edicts.

sentences.zh: 賊敗，與偽中丞崔宣、賊將杜如江、吳希光等十三人，李晟收之，俱斬於安國寺前。

translations.literal: When the rebels were defeated, together with the false Vice Censor Xuan Cui, rebel generals Du Rujiang, Wu Xiguang, and thirteen others, Li Sheng took them and all were executed before Anguo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels fell, Li Sheng seized Yan together with the false Vice Censor Cui Xuan, rebel generals Du Rujiang and Wu Xiguang, and thirteen others. All were executed before Anguo Temple.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：肇分陰陽，爰有生死，修短二事，賢愚一途。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: At the beginning yin and yang were divided, and thus there is life and death; long life and short life are two affairs, but worthy and foolish share one path.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: When yin and yang were first divided, life and death arose. Long life and short life are two fates, but the worthy and the foolish walk the same road.

sentences.zh: 故君子遇夷險之機，不易其節；

translations.literal: Therefore the gentleman, meeting occasions of ease or peril, does not alter his integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the gentleman, whether in ease or peril, does not alter his integrity;

sentences.zh: 小人昧逆順之道，而陷於刑。

translations.literal: the petty man, ignorant of the Way of rebellion and submission, falls into punishment.
translations.idiomatic: the petty man, blind to the way of loyalty and rebellion, falls under the law.

sentences.zh: 鴻毛泰山，斯為至論。

translations.literal: A swan's down feather and Mount Tai—this is the supreme discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Light as a swan's down, heavy as Mount Tai—such is the supreme truth.

sentences.zh: 令言遠總師徒，首為叛逆；

translations.literal: Lingyan from afar commanded master and disciples and was first in rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Lingyan commanded troops from afar and led the rebellion;

sentences.zh: 光晟初當委任，危輸款誠；

translations.literal: Guangcheng at first received appointment and in peril offered sincere submission;
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng, once entrusted with command, offered sincere submission in peril;

sentences.zh: 源休雖曰士流，甚於元惡；

translations.literal: Yuan Xiu, though called a scholar-official, was worse than the chief villain;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu, though a scholar-official by birth, was worse than the chief villain;

sentences.zh: 喬琳巧辭真主，俯就偽官；

translations.literal: Qiao Lin with clever words left the true lord and bowed to accept false office;
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Lin with clever words abandoned the true sovereign and bowed to rebel office;

sentences.zh: 蔣鎮貪祿隳節，皆曰小人。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhen clung to salary and destroyed integrity—all are called petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhen clung to salary and ruined his integrity—all are called petty men.

sentences.zh: 經綸之徒，不足言爾。

translations.literal: Men like Jinglun are not worth speaking of.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Jinglun are scarcely worth mention.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：時爭逆順，命擊死生。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The age contends over rebellion and loyalty; fate strikes at life and death.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: In that age men disputed loyalty and rebellion, and fate struck at life and death.

sentences.zh: 君子守節，小人正刑。

translations.literal: The gentleman keeps integrity; the petty man receives proper punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman keeps his integrity; the petty man meets the law's correction.
